speaker: lucca
personality: Old Quartieri gunsmith, once armorer to the Imperial cohorts, quietly with the cause; respects his craft and plain honesty, bristles at swagger and waste.

openings.text: In. Quickly, and shut the door. The district's crawling with patrols tonight, and I don't need them looking at my shop.
Shop's closed. You're not from here, and you're not Federation. Come in before someone sees you on my step.

exchanges.prompt: My father made rifles for the Imperial cohorts. So did I, for forty years. Now I fix Federation pistols so they leave me alone. What do you want?

replies.text: Ammunition, medkits, smoke. And I can pay.
replies.reaction: Straight to it. All right.

replies.text: Supplies. And to meet the man who still keeps a cohort armorer's bench in the back.
replies.reaction: Not many people know about that bench. Sit down.

replies.text: Whatever you've got. I don't care if it's junk, I just need it fast.
replies.reaction: Nothing in this shop is junk.

exchanges.prompt: Four families on this street have lost someone to the trucks this year. The Federation calls it resettlement. Is that what your people are fighting?

replies.text: Yes. We're trying to find out where they take them, and stop it.
replies.reaction: Good, somebody should. The Ferraro boy was seventeen.

replies.text: I can't talk about what we're fighting.
replies.reaction: Of course not. Never mind, then.

replies.text: We're fighting to win. People get lost in a war.
replies.reaction: People. You say it like it's a number.

exchanges.prompt: One more thing. Whatever I sell you will be used. I need to know it'll be used well.

replies.text: I'll only use it when there's no other way.
replies.reaction: Everyone says that. I hope you mean it.

replies.text: With respect, old man, what I do with it is my business.
replies.reaction: With respect, it's my name stamped on the barrel.

replies.text: It'll go where it counts. And I'll come back and tell you what it did.
replies.reaction: Do that. I'd like to know.

closings.success: All right. Here's what I've got. Take what you need, and go out the back.
closings.failure: No. I don't sell to people who talk like that. Out the back, and remember where you are next time.
closings.rebuff: Not today. Come back when you've thought about who you're talking to.

speaker: lucca
personality: The old gunsmith on second acquaintance; worried about Federation inspectors and his missing neighbors, he wants discretion and the unvarnished truth.

openings.text: You. I remember what you said last time. Say something better or leave.
Back again. Good. I wasn't sure you would be.
There you are. I put a few things aside for you. Friend's price, don't argue.
You made it through. I wondered. Come in, shut the door.

exchanges.prompt: Federation inspectors came on Tuesday. Counted my lathes and asked who I sell to. I told them nobody. Have you told anyone about me?

replies.text: A few people. They're on our side.
replies.reaction: A few people. That's how shops get burned.

replies.text: Only my handler, and only that there's a gunsmith. No name.
replies.reaction: No name. All right, I can live with that.

replies.text: If you're that scared, maybe you should stop selling.
replies.reaction: Scared. I was fixing rifles under shellfire before you were born.

replies.text: No one. You're not in any report, and you won't be.
replies.reaction: I believe you. I don't know why, but I do.

exchanges.prompt: A woman from the street came by. Her son was taken in the spring. She asked if I'd heard where they go. Have you?

replies.text: No.
replies.reaction: No. Nobody has.

replies.text: Not much. They're held at the Castel first. We know that.
replies.reaction: The Castel. When I was a boy, it was a museum.

replies.text: Not enough yet. But I'm looking, and I won't lie to her or to you.
replies.reaction: That's more than the prefecture ever told her.

exchanges.prompt: I'm too old to fight. But I could do more than sell you cartridges. Tell me what would actually help.

replies.text: Keep the shop open and your head down. A safe door in Napoli is worth more than a rifle.
replies.reaction: A safe door. My father would have liked that.

replies.text: Come with us. Pick up a rifle. We need everyone.
replies.reaction: With these hands? Don't be foolish.

replies.text: Listen. People talk in gun shops. Tell me what you hear.
replies.reaction: They do talk. I'll listen harder.

closings.success: Take what you need. And come back. I mean that.
closings.failure: Not today. Something about you today, I don't like it. Go.
closings.rebuff: I'll think about it. Come back next time and we'll see.

speaker: lucca
personality: The gunsmith as an old friend; growing frail and frightened for his street, he wants honesty, proof the agent is a real person, and to know his work outlives him.

openings.text: After last time I nearly didn't open the door. Talk, and choose your words.
You came back. I hoped you would. Let's try that again.
You keep coming back. Good. Every time that door opens and it's you, I know they haven't got you yet.
You keep coming back. Either you're a friend or you're desperate. Sit down and tell me which.
Come in. Your things are on the bench. I've been keeping them back from everyone else.
Come in. Door shut, voice down. You know how it works by now.

exchanges.prompt: Every week there are more trucks and fewer faces on this street. Tell me something true. How is it out there?

replies.text: Worse in the Porto. Better in the Quartieri. We're holding.
replies.reaction: Holding. That's something.

replies.text: Bad. They're taking more people, and we still don't know everything. That's the truth.
replies.reaction: Thank you for not dressing it up.

replies.text: Fine. Nothing for you to worry about.
replies.reaction: Don't manage me. I'm not one of the prefect's clients.

replies.text: I found a transport manifest. It lists people by blood type and tissue match, bound for Pier 9.
replies.reaction: Tissue match is a surgeon's word, not a quartermaster's. What are they doing to those people?

exchanges.prompt: You've never told me your real name. I don't need it. But I'd like to know you still have one.

replies.text: Names get people killed. Why would you even ask?
replies.reaction: Because I'm old, and I like knowing who I'm worrying about.

replies.text: I do. It just isn't the one on my papers.
replies.reaction: Good. Keep it somewhere safe.

replies.text: I have one. When this is over, I'll walk in the front door and tell you myself.
replies.reaction: I'll hold you to that. Make sure there is an over.

exchanges.prompt: My hands shake now. Some days I can't finish a trigger group. One day you'll come and the shop will be shut. What then?

replies.text: Then teach someone first. Your work shouldn't end with you. Napoli will need it after.
replies.reaction: There's a girl on the street who watches me work. Maybe.

replies.text: Then I'll find another gunsmith.
replies.reaction: Honest, at least. Cold, but honest.

replies.text: Then I'll make sure people know what you did for us.
replies.reaction: That's kind. I didn't do it to be remembered.

replies.text: Then you'd better give me a discount while you still can.
replies.reaction: That was a cheap thing to say. Even for this city.

closings.success: Take what you need. Stay alive. That's the only payment I care about.
closings.failure: Not today. I'm too tired for this. Go.
closings.rebuff: Closer. Not there yet. Come back and we'll talk again.
